steps.title: Open User Settings, then Data and Privacy
steps.detail: Scroll to Request all of my data.

steps.title: Choose what to include
steps.detail: Messages, servers and activity are separate tick boxes. Include messages if you want your conversations.

steps.title: Wait up to thirty days
steps.detail: It is usually faster, but Discord makes no promise short of a month.

steps.title: Download within thirty days
steps.detail: The link stays live for a month after it arrives.

notes: Your messages are in the package, which surprises people who expect otherwise - but only yours. A server's conversation is not exported to you, so a thread reads as your half of it with the replies absent. Anything you deleted by hand is gone from Discord and so is absent here too, and the package is a set of JSON files rather than anything readable, so it needs a tool to make sense of.
Only your own messages are included. What other people wrote in the same conversation is not, so an exported chat reads as one half of it.
Attachments are links rather than files, and those links are signed and expire. By the time an old export is opened they are usually dead.
The activity folder is line-separated JSON rather than a JSON array, and for most accounts it is the bulk of the download.

faq.q: Does a Discord data export include other people's messages?
faq.a: No. Only messages you sent. A conversation therefore reads as one side of itself, which surprises most people opening one for the first time.

faq.q: Why are the images in my Discord export missing?
faq.a: Attachments are stored as links rather than files, and Discord signs those links with an expiry. In an export more than a few days old they generally no longer resolve.

faq.q: How long does a Discord data request take?
faq.a: Up to thirty days by Discord's own wording. Most arrive well inside that, and the download link then stays live for another thirty.
